item.title: Oil prices surge after Trump rejects Iran’s plan to reopen Strait of Hormuz
item.description:
Oil prices rose as Washington and Tehran seemed no closer to reaching a durable truce. US President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran on Friday; he told Axios he believed talks would resume this week , though The Wall Street Journal reported that he told aides he expects to bomb Iran again after November’s midterms . All the while, the Trump administration has reportedly been issuing ultimatums to Tehran’s trading partners , warning that continued commerce risked US sanctions. Though oil supplies from the Gulf appear to be recovering — September exports from the Middle East were the highest since the war began — overall sales remain well short of pre-conflict levels. Benchmark crude rose more than 2%. — Prashant Rao

item.title: Powerful nor'easter floods Northeast again, causing problems from New Jersey to New England
item.description:
A powerful storm swept across the Northeast on Saturday, killing at least one person and knocking out power to about 100,000 customers. Leighton Brown, a 56-year-old New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA) employee, was killed in Brooklyn when a tree fell on him during the storm, NYCHA said. “My thoughts are with his entire family as they deal with this unimaginable loss,” New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said . “May he rest in peace, and may his service to our city never be forgotten.” In a separate incident, fire officials said four people were hospitalized with minor injuries after a tree fell on them near a Sheepshead Bay playground. The city’s Parks Department said it had received more than 900 reports of damaged or fallen trees since Friday afternoon, though it cautioned that some may be duplicates. item.title: Mexico's Pacific coast braces for Hurricane Polo
item.description:
Hurricane Nolo is moving away from Hawaiian islands but threat of heavy rain, flash floods and strong winds persists Hurricane Nolo was moving away from the Hawaiian islands on Sunday, but the threat of heavy rain, flash flooding and strong winds persisted in areas of the island chain still recovering from previous storms. Nolo was about 365 miles (585km) south-south-west of Honolulu and moving away from the Big Island at about 12mph (19km/h). But the Hawaii county civil defense agency said a high wind warning, wind advisory and high surf advisory remained in effect for parts of the island through Sunday evening as Nolo’s maximum sustained winds rose to 115mph. item.title: Pope decries 'scourge' of sexual abuse during France visit
item.description:
Pope Leo XIV urged Europe to remember its Christian history and appealed for peace and unity in a speech delivered in France's northeastern city of Metz on Monday, the fourth and final day of his visit. "Relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilised. The value of keeping one's word is dismissed. Instead, people boast of lies and deceit," he said. "Europe can help to break this cycle through the respect for others that it has learned to cultivate and preserve."

item.title: OK, now it’s time for the Patriots to panic about Drake Maye
item.description:
Progress in the NFL is not linear, past success doesn't guarantee future success, regression to the mean is normal and expected—all of the cliches in the world can't possibly rationalize whatever the hell is happening to Drake Maye and the New England Patriots so far this season. Currently sitting at 1-2 after Jacksonville laid down a 35-6 " old-fashioned ass whooping ," as Pats safety Kevin Byard III put it, New England is finding life after a division title and a shock Super Bowl run to be, somehow, even harder and more dispiriting that it seemed on paper. Some fall-off was to be expected after a season in which the Pats had the easiest schedule of the century, but what's become of Drake Maye, who looked like a perennial MVP candidate last season, is downright shocking. item.title: French Senate elections: What next after far right surge?
item.description:
Marine Le Pen hails ‘historic victory’ as her party and allies win enough seats to form caucus just months ahead of presidential poll The French far-right leader Marine Le Pen has said her 2027 presidential campaign will be boosted after her anti-immigration party, the National Rally (RN), and its allies secured a record 14 seats in partial senate elections this weekend. Le Pen called the results a “historic victory” and “major milestone” after her party cleared the 10-seat threshold to be able to form a senate group for the first time, following an indirect vote by local officials including mayors and councillors. item.title: Cattle to feed: Why a global meat crisis is looming
item.description:
This story was originally published by the Guardian and is reproduced here as part of the Climate Desk collaboration. Two decades after the release of his groundbreaking documentary An Inconvenient Truth , Al Gore has admitted he was surprised by the ferocious, ongoing backlash from the fossil fuel industry and its political allies. But the former US vice-president insists he still has optimism the world will confront the climate crisis. item.title: Serbia's populist President Vucic resigns to run for PM
item.description:
Serbia’s populist President Aleksandar Vucic resigned Sunday to pursue a bid to become prime minister in an upcoming early parliamentary election that will test his firm rule in the Balkan country, which was rattled by nearly two years of protests.
